renethack @VERSION@: the complete source
========================================

The source of the game this archive came with, as the NetHack General
Public License asks of a copy distributed in executable form (its 3(a)):
renethack's client, its engine host and its patches to NetHack, NetHack
itself, the Lua release it links, and their build. All of it is under the
NetHack General Public License (LICENSE), but for the parts NOTICE lists.

What is where
-------------
client/rust/          the Godot extension and the crates it is made of (Rust)
client/godot/         the Godot project: its scene, settings, shaders, fonts
                      and interface; the art's and the sounds' manifests,
                      sources and credits
client/i18n/          the catalogs of the game's texts and their translations
client/help/          the in-game help: NetHack's Guidebook
client/achievements/  the achievements
engine/upstream/      NetHack 5.0.0 as released, unchanged; its commit is in
                      engine/upstream.rev
engine/patches/       renethack's changes to NetHack, which the build applies
                      in the order of engine/patches/series; every file they
                      change says so, with the date
engine/host/          the protocol host the engine is built with
engine/lua-*/         the Lua release NetHack links (MIT licence)
tools/, Makefile      the tools and the build; tools/dist/ makes the packages
steam/                what Steamworks takes: the achievements, the upload
                      scripts

Not here
--------
The art and the sounds (client/godot/art/, client/godot/audio/) and the
pictures for Steam (steam/store/, steam/achievements/, steam/icon/). They
are not the program but works under their own licences, CC0 and CC-BY,
listed in client/godot/art/CREDITS.md and client/godot/audio/CREDITS.md.
The game holds them; `make art` and `make audio` fetch them again from the
sources in client/godot/art/sources.json and client/godot/audio/sources.json
and check them against the locks beside those.

Godot Engine, which runs the game (4.7.2, MIT licence, godotengine.org;
tools/dist/fetch_godot.sh fetches it), and the Rust crates the extension
links, which cargo fetches as client/rust/Cargo.lock lists them.

Building
--------
On macOS or Linux, with a C compiler, GNU make and patch:

    make -C engine

builds NetHack with the patches and the host into engine/build/ (nh-engine,
recover and data/) from these files alone, with neither git nor the
network. With Rust (stable, 1.94 or newer):

    cd client/rust && cargo build --release --locked -p renethack-gd

builds the extension (cargo fetches the crates); `cargo test` runs the
client's tests, of which those that check the art and the sounds against
their manifests need them. With Godot 4.7, `make run GODOT=<its binary>`
plays the game: without the art and the sounds it runs with stand-ins and
in silence; `make art` and `make audio` bring them. `make dist-macos` (on a
Mac) and `make dist-linux` (on Linux, in the Steam Linux Runtime 3 SDK)
package it as the game you have. README.md says the rest.
